FX-GLDISP-001.says: 32 bpc (After Effects), Glow in After Effects units at tutorial 2's kind of setting, threshold 0, radius 4, intensity 0.1: worked in display values, D-746: each channel's light 0.1 x 16 / 3 times its display value, spread at sigma 1.6, laid on at strength 1 with the covering as blurred, so the halo covers more than Float's.

FX-GLDISP-002.says: 32 bpc (After Effects), tutorial 2's glow layer in small: Solid Composite on black, then the same Glow. Opaque, the glow lifts the black round the patches with their own colours.

FX-GLDISP-003.says: 32 bpc (After Effects), Glow with tint #ff4000, threshold 0, intensity 0.2: the tint is used as written, a display value, so read straight in display values the halo is #ff4000 times 0.2 x 16 / 3, held at 1 (D-746).

FX-GLDISP-004.says: 32 bpc (After Effects), Glow in classic units, FX-GLOW-001's settings: D-89's strength, worked in display values.

FX-GLDISP-005.says: 32 bpc (After Effects), Glow in After Effects units with Screen: held inside 0 to 1 and screened, in display values.

FX-GLDISP-006.says: 8 bpc, Glow in After Effects units at After Effects' defaults, threshold 60, radius 10, intensity 1: in display values by D-746's rule, then held to 8 bits, so nothing passes white.

FX-GLDISP-007.says: Float, FX-GLDISP-001's Glow: linear light and D-331's rule as before, FX-GLOW-AE-004 exactly.

FX-GLDISP-008.says: 32 bpc (After Effects), the half-covering patches with Solid Composite #3c286e at opacity 50 and nothing else: laid on in display values, the purple used as written.
